chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the maintenance of a pregnant woman whose husband dies, it is from all the wealth until she gives birth. This report can be understood in two ways: one is that it is recommended if the heirs agree to it; and the second is that the ruling is that she is maintained from all the wealth because the share of the fetus has not yet been distinguished, and it is only distinguished when she gives birth, at which point it is known whether it is male or female, and then his share is separated. When it is distinguished, what was spent on her is taken from his share and returned to the heirs. The benefit of the report is that maintenance does not fall upon one heir to the exclusion of the other, but they are all equal in that. As for the slave woman, if she is a wife and is the mother of her master's child, and her husband dies, her waiting period is the same as that of the free woman. And if she is a slave who is not the mother of a child, her waiting period is two months and five days. The apparent meaning of the Verse indicates the first case, and it is general for all wives, and there is no distinction between a free woman and a slave in it. And it is not obligatory for us to do so, because we only specify it with what we mention later from the reports, and also it has been narrated.

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَد: Mother of a child (concubine who bears her master's child)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a slave woman who is the mother of her master's child after her husband's death?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents two scholarly interpretations for the financial maintenance of a pregnant widow: either as a recommended act (istihbab) if heirs agree, or as a mandatory deduction from the general estate since the fetus's share is not yet distinct. The text further clarifies that a slave wife who is a 'mother of a child' (umm walad) observes the same waiting period (iddah) as a free woman, supported by the general applicability of Quranic verses to all wives.
